The Great Commentary and Sub-commentary on the *Complete Enlightenment Sūtra* (*Yuánjué jīng*) as expounded by my ancestor, Zen Master Guìfēng, were carved into woodblocks in the land of Haedong; however, the handwritten copies in this region still contain many errors and corruptions. During the Shàoxīng era, there was... [text fragment] ...who... [text fragment] ...[had them corrected].

The lecturer Enjō (byname Gishō) sought out an Indian manuscript and, having raised funds for its publication, established the topical outline (*kō*) for the *Sho-shō*. However, he only completed the outline for the first fascicle; before the woodblocks for the remaining sections were finished, he passed away. Consequently, while I was leading my disciples at the Ancient Pagoda in Kashō, I read through this abbreviated version repeatedly.
